newsitem.title: USA: DC control board opposes mayor's FY'98 budget plan.
newsitem.headline: DC control board opposes mayor's FY'98 budget plan.

text.p: The District of Columbia's financial control board said Friday it opposes a proposal by D.C. Mayor Marion Barry to balance the city's budget in fiscal 1998 by restructuring millions in D.C. debt.
Andrew Brimmer, chairman of the city's five member board, said that relying on debt restructuring at this time would only "camouflage" the city's grave budget problems.
Instead of restructuring its debt, the city should "restructure" its budget by making deeper cuts in D.C. spending, Brimmer said in a press statement.
Barry last weekend proposed a $3.3 billion budget in fiscal 1998 for D.C., the first balanced budget since the city's five-member congressionally appointed control board took office.
Barry's budget calls for $50 million in savings by extending the city's multi-million-dollar outstanding debt through restructuring.

The city is required by Congress to balance its budget in fiscal 1999, but the mayor, control board and other city officials want to balance it a year earlier to impress Capitol Hill, which is studying a proposed $3.9 billion relief package for D.C. proposed by President Clinton. Brimmer said he is not vetoing future D.C. debt restructurings.
"Restructurings do have legitimate public finance aims, despite long-term costs," he said.
Brimmer said he is particularly "troubled" by the Barry plan because, while it "balances" D.C.'s budget in fiscal 1998, it forecasts a deficit in each of the next three fiscal years.
Such forecasts would violate the federal law that created the financial control board, Brimmer said.
Brimmer said that, before he will approve any future debt restructuring, D.C. must present a "thorough analysis" showing it will apply proceeds to capital projects.
And D.C. would have to pledge to focus proceeds first on those infrastructure projects that have been backlogged, Brimmer said.
